chapters.screenText: Run Icepack from your HDF5 fields, then save the results.
chapters.screenWhy: Keep the source inputs, inspect native fields, and save a complete result package.
chapters.expectedResult: Have run.py, initial_fields.py and icepack-shelf-initial.h5 ready.
chapters.title: Your goal: initialize and run Icepack
instructions: Run a synthetic shelf from your own gridded fields, then save the initial/final maps and native results.
Download run.py, initial_fields.py and icepack-shelf-initial.h5 from this tutorial page.
chapters.note: Start with your approved cloud account already connected and its cloud resources prepared.
chapters.why: Keep the source inputs, inspect native fields, and save a complete result package.

chapters.screenText: Start here in CryoLauncher. Choose Cloud for this tutorial.
chapters.screenWhy: An owned example keeps scripts, dataset references and results together.
chapters.expectedResult: Your workspace keeps scripts, datasets, run history and results together.
chapters.title: Start here
instructions: Open CryoLauncher and sign in. Use an approved connected cloud account with its resources prepared.
The following steps select this tutorial’s model and example.
chapters.note: Shared application orientation; the case-specific configuration follows.
chapters.why: An owned example keeps scripts, dataset references and results together.

chapters.screenText: Choose Cloud → Advanced.
chapters.screenWhy: Cloud uses your connected account; Advanced enables your owned scripts and datasets.
chapters.expectedResult: Use the editable workspace for your own scripts and datasets.
chapters.title: 1. Open the cloud workspace
instructions: Choose Cloud → Advanced → Icepack.
You will create a separate workspace example for this HDF5 run.
chapters.note: Keep the three supplied tutorial files together on your computer.
chapters.why: Cloud uses your connected account; Advanced enables your owned scripts and datasets.

chapters.screenText: Choose Icepack. Next, create a new workspace example.
chapters.screenWhy: The selected example controls the source files and dataset references used for launch.
chapters.expectedResult: The next step gives your HDF5 run a separate name.
chapters.title: 1. Open the cloud workspace
instructions: Choose Icepack as the model.
Next, create a new owned workspace example with a separate name for this HDF5 run.
chapters.note: Keep the three supplied tutorial files together on your computer.
chapters.why: The selected example controls the source files and dataset references used for launch.

chapters.screenText: Enter a new name and choose New example.
chapters.screenWhy: An owned workspace separates your files from the supplied application example.
chapters.expectedResult: Wait for the created-workspace message and empty file list.
chapters.title: 2. Create your own example
instructions: Enter a new name, then choose New example.
The new example has an empty file list, ready for your Python files.
chapters.note: The recorded example is pilot-icepack-h5-1118.
chapters.why: An owned workspace separates your files from the supplied application example.

chapters.screenText: Choose run.py and initial_fields.py in your file picker; Open.
chapters.screenWhy: Selection picks local files; importing is the step that saves them in this example.
chapters.expectedResult: Check that two script files are selected.
chapters.title: 3. Select both Python files
instructions: Choose script files. In your file picker, select run.py and initial_fields.py, then choose Open.
Check that the button now shows two selected files.
chapters.note: You will import both files into the same workspace example.
chapters.why: Selection picks local files; importing is the step that saves them in this example.

chapters.screenText: Choose Import script files.
chapters.screenWhy: Import saves the selected source files; it does not submit a model run.
chapters.expectedResult: Enable Replace existing script files if run.py already exists.
chapters.title: 4. Import the selected scripts
instructions: Choose Import script files.
chapters.note: If your example already contains run.py, enable Replace existing script files first.
chapters.why: Import saves the selected source files; it does not submit a model run.

chapters.screenText: Check the imported filenames and saved status.
chapters.screenWhy: Import saves the selected source files; it does not submit a model run.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: Imported run.py, initial_fields.py. Files are saved.
chapters.title: 4. Check both saved filenames
instructions: Wait for Imported run.py, initial_fields.py. Files are saved.
The file selector now contains run.py; the import confirmation lists both imported files.
chapters.note: For seeded or existing files, use Replace existing script files before importing.
chapters.why: Import saves the selected source files; it does not submit a model run.

chapters.screenText: Set the Run target to run.py.
chapters.screenWhy: Run target selects the entry script; other imported files can act as helpers.
chapters.expectedResult: The script calls initial_fields.py to read and validate your HDF5 input.
chapters.title: 5. Use run.py as the entry point
instructions: Set Run target to run.py.
This script calls initial_fields.py to validate and read your HDF5 input.
chapters.note: Importing files saves them; launching is a separate step.
chapters.why: Run target selects the entry script; other imported files can act as helpers.

chapters.screenText: Choose data files; select icepack-shelf-initial.h5, then Open.
chapters.screenWhy: Selecting a file prepares it for upload; it is not in the dataset registry yet.
chapters.expectedResult: Check that one data file is selected.
chapters.title: 6. Choose your HDF5 input
instructions: In Datasets choose Choose data files.
In your file picker select icepack-shelf-initial.h5 and choose Open. Check that one file is selected.
chapters.note: Next, upload the selected file into your workspace.
chapters.why: Selecting a file prepares it for upload; it is not in the dataset registry yet.

chapters.screenText: Choose Upload; wait for the HDF5 filename.
chapters.screenWhy: Upload stores the dataset; the script must read its fields to initialize the model.
chapters.expectedResult: Expected: Uploaded: icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
chapters.title: 7. Upload the selected data file
instructions: Choose Upload. Wait for Uploaded: icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
Check that the new HDF5 filename appears in your dataset list.
chapters.note: The supplied file contains full thickness, base, surface, vx, vy and floating-mask grids.
chapters.why: Upload stores the dataset; the script must read its fields to initialize the model.

chapters.screenText: Select the HDF5 dataset and choose Reference in example.
chapters.screenWhy: A reference stages the chosen dataset under data/ when this example launches.
chapters.expectedResult: Use icepack-shelf-initial.h5 as the reference alias.
chapters.title: 8. Reference the file in this example
instructions: Select icepack-shelf-initial.h5. Keep that filename as the reference alias, then choose Reference in example.
chapters.note: Your script will read data/icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
chapters.why: A reference stages the chosen dataset under data/ when this example launches.

chapters.screenText: Confirm the reference saved in this example.
chapters.screenWhy: A reference stages the chosen dataset under data/ when this example launches.
chapters.expectedResult: Your script will read data/icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
chapters.title: 8. Confirm the staged data path
instructions: Read the reference confirmation: data/icepack-shelf-initial.h5.
When you launch, CryoLauncher copies the selected dataset into that path for run.py to read.
chapters.note: The reference is attached to your current workspace example.
chapters.why: A reference stages the chosen dataset under data/ when this example launches.

chapters.screenText: Choose Review & Launch.
chapters.screenWhy: Review is the checkpoint for the selected case, inputs, resources and charges.
chapters.expectedResult: Review the model, example and run target before submitting.
chapters.title: 9. Review your configuration
instructions: Choose Review & Launch.
Before submitting, check that the summary names your intended model and workspace example.
chapters.note: Review the current settings before you launch.
chapters.why: Review is the checkpoint for the selected case, inputs, resources and charges.

chapters.screenText: Confirm ICEPACK and pilot-icepack-h5-1118.
chapters.screenWhy: Confirm the intended model and owned example before submitting the run.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep run.py as the entry point with the HDF5 reference attached.
chapters.title: 9. Check the HDF5 run summary
instructions: Check Model: ICEPACK and Example: pilot-icepack-h5-1118.
Keep run.py as the entry point, with the referenced HDF5 input attached.
chapters.note: This native run used 2 vCPU and 8 GiB.
chapters.why: Confirm the intended model and owned example before submitting the run.

chapters.screenText: Control guide: choose Launch cloud run when checks are Ready.
chapters.screenWhy: Confirmation starts a paid cloud run using the reviewed configuration.
chapters.expectedResult: The following card belongs to this tutorial’s original native run.
chapters.title: 9. Launch when the checks are ready
instructions: Choose Launch cloud run when the readiness checks are ready.
chapters.note: Control guide; the original accepted HDF5 run follows.
chapters.why: Confirmation starts a paid cloud run using the reviewed configuration.

chapters.screenText: Follow your new HDF5 run card.
chapters.screenWhy: Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.
chapters.expectedResult: Wait for completion; opening another tab does not cancel the job.
chapters.title: 9. Follow the new run card
instructions: Your HDF5 run now has its own Cloud Run card.
Wait for the job to finish; opening another tab does not cancel it.
chapters.note: This run used 2 vCPU and 8 GiB. Queue/startup and model timings are reported separately.
chapters.why: Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.

chapters.screenText: When the job shows Completed, open View results.
chapters.screenWhy: Completion lets you retrieve and inspect this run’s saved native output.
chapters.expectedResult: This script runs one 0.01-year step with zero accumulation.
chapters.title: 10. Open the completed results
instructions: When the run shows Completed, open View results.
The native script performs one 0.01-year step with zero accumulation.
chapters.note: Next, render and save the fields from this completed HDF5 run.
chapters.why: Completion lets you retrieve and inspect this run’s saved native output.

chapters.screenText: Choose Render for the selected field.
chapters.screenWhy: The solution, field name and units identify what you are about to view.
chapters.expectedResult: You can inspect thickness or velocity after the native run finishes.
chapters.title: 11. Render a native field
instructions: Choose Render to draw the selected field.
chapters.note: You can switch between thickness and velocity after the run finishes.
chapters.why: The solution, field name and units identify what you are about to view.

chapters.screenText: Choose solution icepack, select a field, then Render.
chapters.screenWhy: The solution, field name and units identify what you are viewing.
chapters.expectedResult: Velocity is in metres/year; thickness is in metres.
chapters.title: 11. Render a native field
instructions: In Results choose solution icepack, choose velocity or thickness, then choose Render.
Use the field name and units to interpret the plot.
chapters.note: Velocity is in metres/year; thickness is in metres.
chapters.why: The solution, field name and units identify what you are viewing.

chapters.screenText: Open initial-conditions.png to inspect the initialized fields.
chapters.screenWhy: The saved initial map lets you inspect what was sampled from the uploaded grid.
chapters.expectedResult: The uploaded 5 × 9 grid was sampled at all 25 native mesh vertices.
chapters.title: 12. Inspect the initialized fields
instructions: Open initial-conditions.png in your saved results.
It shows thickness, surface and speed sampled from your uploaded grid onto the native mesh.
chapters.note: The supplied grid has 5 × 9 points and covers a 10 km × 10 km synthetic shelf.
chapters.why: The saved initial map lets you inspect what was sampled from the uploaded grid.

chapters.screenText: Open the final saved thickness map.
chapters.screenWhy: Use the colour scale and units to interpret the solved native thickness.
chapters.expectedResult: Final area-weighted mean: 403.649861 m; domain RMS speed: 133.908461 m/year.
chapters.title: 13. Inspect the final thickness
instructions: Open the final thickness figure and compare the colour scale with the initial map.
Final thickness is 300.022696–499.980847 m; its area-weighted mean is 403.649861 m.
chapters.note: The final domain RMS speed is 133.908461 m/year.
chapters.why: Use the colour scale and units to interpret the solved native thickness.

chapters.screenText: Choose Download results for this run.
chapters.screenWhy: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.
chapters.expectedResult: Wait for a fresh HTTPS download link.
chapters.title: 14. Generate your download link
instructions: Choose Download results.
Wait for a new HTTPS download link for the current run.
chapters.note: Use the freshly generated link to save the ZIP.
chapters.why: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.

chapters.screenText: Open the new HTTPS link and save your results ZIP.
chapters.screenWhy: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep all 12 archive members with your scripts and HDF5 input.
chapters.title: 14. Keep the result archive
instructions: Open the generated HTTPS link to save your results ZIP.
It contains the mesh, native fields, initial/final figures, metrics and runtime/RNG provenance.
chapters.note: Keep this 12-member archive and its manifest with your input files.
chapters.why: The archive keeps this run’s numeric outputs, figures and provenance together.

chapters.screenText: Keep the inputs, figures, native fields and run provenance together.
chapters.screenWhy: Keep the scientific qualifications and provenance with the accepted result.
chapters.expectedResult: Initial-field interpolation matched independently at every native node.
chapters.title: What this completed example establishes
instructions: The five initialized fields matched an independent interpolation at all 25 native nodes; the mesh has 32 triangles.
These portable CG1 fields are numeric results, rather than a Firedrake checkpoint. This example is not an independent native repeat or an accuracy assessment.
chapters.note: Submission → Batch start: 214.703 s; task: 46.352 s; script: 16.9818 s. Long waits are shortened in the video.
chapters.why: Keep the scientific qualifications and provenance with the accepted result.
